name: Humanitarian funding gap
summary: WFP says funding cuts removed 900,000 people in Sudan from food aid by 12 Nov; caseload cuts, not a full suspension
state: WFP said on 12 Nov that funding shortfalls cut the number it reaches in Sudan from over 4 million in August to just over 3 million, with about 900,000 people losing food aid, and that it needs $520m to reach 5.4 million people to April 2027 (UN News). Darfur24 reported that the cuts began in September. In October, UN News reported that funding cuts left about half a million people in Gaza without WFP food assistance. These are major caseload cuts, not a formal large-scale suspension, so Watch is kept with a worsening trend.
for_you: People in Sudan's famine-risk areas, Gaza and refugee camps are most exposed to aid cuts. Smaller caseloads tend to raise malnutrition and push more people to move. OCHA's Financial Tracking Service shows funding by country.
rubric_hit: Watch: major ration and caseload cuts (WFP Sudan 900,000 cut, 12 Nov); no large-scale suspension in famine-risk countries

why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.
